versioning_policy: RiboShift releases are immutable benchmark snapshots. Source additions, normalization-rule changes, and split-policy changes require a new release version.
redistribution_scope: Normalized benchmark tables, split assignments, matched-decoy candidates, schemas, summaries, and metadata generated for RiboShift.

croissant_metadata.notes: Croissant metadata is distributed as a separate upload package.

responsible_ai.intended_use: Evaluation of RNA-small molecule interaction models under controlled biological and chemical novelty settings.
responsible_ai.usage_info: The main cross-model comparison uses the direct_only view with matched-decoy ranking.
responsible_ai.conditions_of_access: RiboShift tables are released as normalized benchmark artifacts; upstream source assets remain subject to their original terms.
responsible_ai.maintenance: RiboShift releases are immutable benchmark snapshots. Source additions, normalization-rule changes, and split-policy changes require a new release version.
responsible_ai.sensitive_data: The released benchmark tables contain no direct personal data.
gaps_and_biases: The direct_only benchmark view is small and long-tailed.
RNA family coverage is incomplete and may rely on cluster90 proxies.
Generated decoys are not experimentally validated negatives.
Disease and functional taxonomy coverage is not standardized across sources.

licensing.benchmark_artifact_license_scope: Applies to newly created RiboShift benchmark artifacts: normalized benchmark tables, split assignments, matched-decoy candidates, schemas, summaries, metadata, and benchmark-specific documentation.
licensing.upstream_source_constraints: Upstream source datasets remain subject to their original licenses, terms of use, and attribution requirements.

known_limitations: The direct_only view is modest in size and strongly long-tailed.
RNA grouping falls back to cluster90 proxies when Rfam coverage is unavailable.
Matched decoys are generated candidates rather than experimentally validated negatives.
No unified disease or function taxonomy is available across all direct-evidence sources.
